why: The closed vocabulary every scenario in this directory is written in: the six verbs of the harness contract, the events a harness may produce, and the codes a harness may answer with when it cannot produce one. Both readers load this file first and refuse a scenario that steps outside it — which is what stops the set growing a word only one language understands.

message.why: One whole thing the agent said, at a protocol boundary.

tool_use.why: A step the room shows while it is happening.

step_failed.why: That step came back an error. It marks the step already on the timeline rather than adding one — and it is NOT the event a tool that returned produces, which is the whole of #1096.

step_output.why: What that step handed back, for whoever opens its line. Written onto the step already on the timeline, never a line of its own; the room keeps only a capped tail.

tool_result.why: A subagent's conclusion, as its own event: it otherwise reaches only the thread that spawned it. Every other return is written onto its step (step_output).

session_info.why: The harness's own name for this conversation, announced before the turn ends so a turn that dies mid-stream still leaves something to resume.

result.why: This turn is over. The platform's transcript pass is keyed off it, which is what makes 「每轮结束前增量上交」 a property of the turn rather than of a timer.

subagent_start.why: A second worker inside one session began.

subagent_stop.why: A second worker handed something back. Not 「done」.

retrying.why: A model request failed and the harness is sending it again. Nothing else reaches the room while it waits, so without this a turn stuck in backoff looks exactly like a turn that is thinking. Every field is optional: a harness says as much of the count as it knows.

differences.no-subagent-threads: This harness runs no second worker inside a session, so nothing can be attributed to one.
differences.no-subagent-tool-return: This harness reports that a subagent stopped, but never what it handed back as a tool return.
differences.no-session-id-of-its-own: This harness does not announce a conversation id separately from the turn that ends; the platform learns it with the result.
